title: Usage insights: top cost drivers heuristics + explainability copy
author: Nadia Rahman
body:
Summary: Implements the first pass of the Top cost drivers + What changed? backend for In-console usage insights. Adds heuristic scoring for common cost deltas (token out growth, cache hit-rate drop, retries/fallbacks, model mix shifts, longer contexts, streaming overhead) and returns explainability strings suitable for direct rendering in the Console. Includes a fixture-based test suite for delta scenarios and guardrails to avoid misleading output.

Context: This is the service-side component for ENG-3819 (Top cost drivers service) and unblocks the console cards/table work in the beta. We intentionally keep the output explainable and non-causal (“likely drivers”) and include confidence/coverage checks. Reconciliation vs billing totals is handled elsewhere (ENG-3817), but this change ensures we only explain changes when the underlying aggregated totals are within tolerance.

API shape (response excerpt): Adds `drivers[]` to the existing breakdown delta response used by the insights console. Each driver contains: `driver_code`, `title`, `summary`, `details`, `estimated_impact_usd`, `estimated_impact_pct`, `direction` (increase|decrease), and `confidence` (low|medium|high). Copy strings are generated server-side so that UX doesn’t have to re-implement heuristics-specific wording.

Heuristics implemented (v1): 1) TOKENS_OUT_DELTA: Detects week-over-week increase in output tokens as a primary spend driver; provides a context-length distribution note when p90 context increases in the same window. 2) CACHE_HIT_RATE_DROP: Attributes increased spend to lower cache effectiveness (prefix/KV cache miss). Includes the miss delta and a reminder that cache effectiveness is sensitive to prompt variation and routing changes. 3) RETRIES_INCREASE: Uses metering retry_count and request_count deltas to flag increased retries; suppresses if retry attribution coverage < 95% for the selected route/model. 4) FALLBACK_RATE_INCREASE: Flags increased fallback usage (e.g., model variant fallback due to capacity) and estimates impact by comparing effective blended unit price across the two windows. 5) MODEL_MIX_SHIFT: For a route rollup, highlights when traffic shifted toward higher unit-cost models (family/version bucketing aware). 6) STREAMING_OVERHEAD: When streaming is enabled and average chunk count per request increases, flags potential overhead (extra tokens and/or compute) with a caveat that it may be intentional for UX latency. 7) LATENCY_CORRELATED_SPEND: When p95 latency grows alongside spend for the same tokens, flags likely compute inefficiency (e.g., longer decode, lower batching) and points to Optimize levers; this is confidence=low unless the correlation exceeds the threshold and request volume is sufficient.

Guardrails / correctness constraints: - Only emit drivers when baseline volumes meet minimum thresholds (default: >= 500 requests OR >= $50 spend in the comparison window) to reduce noise. - Suppress drivers when attribution coverage is low for required fields (route_tag/model_bucket/cache fields). - Suppress driver ranking when reconciliation drift (aggregated totals vs billing hook totals) exceeds the configured tolerance for the workspace/time range; return a single driver: DATA_INCOMPLETE with a friendly message and action (“Try a shorter range” / “Data is still processing”). - All “impact” estimates are bounded to the observed total delta and we clamp negative impacts to 0 for increase-only drivers.

Explainability copy: Copy is centralized in `TopDriversCopy.ts` (server) with simple templating and localized number formatting. Titles are short and stable (used as keys for future i18n). The `details` field is written to be finance-friendly (explicitly states the metric deltas) and includes a non-causal disclaimer where appropriate.

Tests: Adds fixture-driven tests under `packages/usage-insights/top-drivers/__fixtures__/` representing common real-world deltas: - token_out_spike_simple.json - cache_hit_drop_with_stable_tokens_in.json - model_mix_shift_aliases.json (regression coverage for model alias bucketing) - retries_increase_partial_coverage.json (ensures suppression) - fallback_increase_blended_price.json - latency_correlation_low_confidence.json - data_incomplete_reconciliation_drift.json (matches SUP-24811 patterns) Each fixture includes input aggregates for window A/B and expected sorted drivers with impact/clamped values and exact copy strings (with stable formatting).

Implementation notes: - Driver computation is pure and deterministic; we pass in pre-aggregated metrics for a route/model (or route rollup) and a comparison spec. - Ranking is by estimated_impact_usd (primary) then confidence then code tie-breaker for stability. - Added a small `formatDelta()` helper to keep copy consistent across drivers.

Files / modules touched (high-level): - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/computeDrivers.ts - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/driverCodes.ts - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/copy/TopDriversCopy.ts - services/usage-insights/src/topDrivers/thresholds.ts - services/usage-insights/src/routes/v1/usageInsightsDeltas.ts (wire drivers into response) - services/usage-insights/test/topDrivers/*.test.ts - services/usage-insights/test/topDrivers/__fixtures__/*.json

Rollout: Feature-gated by `usage_insights_top_drivers` (server-side). Console will ignore the field if absent; safe to merge ahead of UI. This PR does not change storage/aggregation schema.

Follow-ups: - Tune thresholds with beta feedback (especially for low-volume workspaces). - Consider splitting streaming overhead into token vs request overhead once we have consistent chunk telemetry across regions. - Add docs links in `details` once the docs URL is finalized by DevEx.

Screenshots: N/A (backend only).

Changelog / release notes: Internal-only beta capability; no public changelog entry yet.
commits: topDrivers: add driver codes + scoring framework
topDrivers: add server-side copy templates + number formatting
api: include drivers[] in deltas response behind feature flag
tests: add fixture-based delta scenarios + snapshot expectations
chore: tighten lint rules and export boundaries in usage-insights service
conversation:
Logan Wright (review): The pure function approach is good. Two questions: (1) can we guarantee driver ordering stability when impacts are near-equal due to rounding? (2) can we avoid emitting MODEL_MIX_SHIFT for route+model views (it’s only meaningful for route rollups).

Nadia Rahman (author): (1) Added secondary sort keys (confidence then driver_code) and we rank on unrounded impact_usd internally. (2) Agreed; I gated MODEL_MIX_SHIFT to only run when the query scope is route_rollup.

Chloe Martin (review): Copy: the “cache miss” wording is a bit accusatory. Can we make it clearer that it may be expected if prompts vary? Also, we should include the cache hit-rate before/after in the details.

Nadia Rahman (author): Updated CACHE_HIT_RATE_DROP details to include “Hit rate: 62% → 41%” and added a note about prompt variability + routing changes. Also softened the title from “Cache misses increased” to “Cache hit rate dropped”.

Allison Grant (review): Please add a guardrail so we don’t report latency-correlated spend unless we have enough samples. Also, can you add metrics coverage checks for retries/fallbacks? We’ve seen partial coverage in streaming endpoints in one region.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added min sample size for LATENCY_CORRELATED_SPEND (default 1k requests) and coverage gating for retry_count/fallback_count presence. Added fixture `retries_increase_partial_coverage.json` to ensure suppression.

Markus Klein (review): From customer calls, people will ask “is this causal?”. Suggest including an explicit disclaimer in the driver details and a link to docs later.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added a standard disclaimer line for low/medium confidence drivers (“This is a correlation based on observed telemetry; validate in your app logs.”). I left a TODO hook for docs URLs to be injected when available.

Chloe Martin (review): One more thing: impacts should never exceed the observed total delta for the scope; otherwise it reads wrong.

Nadia Rahman (author): Implemented clamping so sum of driver impacts is bounded by total_delta_usd and individual impacts cannot exceed delta_usd.

Allison Grant (approval): Looks good with guardrails + fixtures.

Logan Wright (approval): Approved; thanks for adding deterministic ordering.

Merge: Squash merged by Nadia Rahman after green CI.
